what: Anything dplyr can express is a rule
title: Get started with expectr
text: checkpoints register work:
code: # Identifiers must look right (a missing cvr is a separate rule) df |>   expect_none(!is.na(cvr) & !grepl("^\\d{8}$", cvr),               abort_msg = "Malformed CVR numbers")  # CPR numbers must hold a real date of birth (add_cpr_info() is from daos) df |>   daos::add_cpr_info(cpr, valid) |>   expect_none(!valid, warn_msg = "Invalid CPR numbers")  # Spells must not end before they start spells |>   expect_none(end < start, abort_msg = "Spells ending before they start")  # Amounts must reconcile within tolerance df |>   expect_none(abs(total - rowSums(across(starts_with("post_")))) > 1,               warn_msg = "Totals do not reconcile")  # Categorical values must be in the codebook df |>   expect_none(!branche %in% codebook$branche, abort_msg = "Unknown industry codes")  # Every expected unit must be present (anti-join as violation set) expected |>   anti_join(df, by = "cvr") |>   expect_empty(warn_msg = "Units missing from the delivery")

title: Get started with expectr
text: chain checkpoints stops first abort. delivery five problems, want hear five one go, one per run. tally keep count, tally marks dplyr::tally(). whole idea tally_violations(): evaluates every rule counts violating rows, never warns stops. Counting judging kept apart. expect_*() functions judge; tally counts, severity decided afterwards. rows column holds row numbers rule’s violations, starwars[report$rows[[1]], ]. Filtered rules failed, tally violation set, goes straight checkpoint: Kept unfiltered, validation report can sent back whoever made data, e.g. report |> select(-rows) |> daos::write_excel(...).
code: report <- starwars |>   tally_violations(     "Missing species"   = is.na(species),     "Taller than 2.5 m" = height > 250,     "Heavier than 1 t"  = mass > 1000,     "Negative height"   = height < 0   ) report #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   rule                  n rows      #>   <chr>             <int> <list>    #> 1 Missing species       4 <int [4]> #> 2 Taller than 2.5 m     1 <int [1]> #> 3 Heavier than 1 t      1 <int [1]> #> 4 Negative height       0 <int [0]> report |>   filter(n > 0) |>   expect_empty(warn_msg = "The data failed validation") #> Warning in expect_empty(filter(report, n > 0), warn_msg = "The data failed validation"): The data failed validation #> ℹ 3 rows found: #>     rule                  n rows #>     <chr>             <int> <list> #>   1 Missing species       4 <int [4]> #>   2 Taller than 2.5 m     1 <int [1]> #>   3 Heavier than 1 t      1 <int [1]>

what: Unattended pipelines: log, dump and catch
title: Get started with expectr
text: pipelines run unattended, every checkpoint can append line log write offending rows CSV file. Set top script options instead repeating paths every check: check ran named log, failures say many rows broke rule, rows waiting dump directory. CSV files written byte order mark, Excel shows æ, ø å correctly. failed check signals condition class expectr_failure carries offending rows $violations. Code react failure, rather just stop, can catch :
code: options(   expectr.log  = format(Sys.time(), "log/%Y%m%d_%H%M%S_checks.log"),   expectr.dump = "log/violations" )  df |>   expect_none(is.na(id), abort_msg = "NA ids") |>   expect_none(amount < 0, warn_msg = "Negative amounts") |>   expect_unique(id, year, warn_msg = "Duplicate person-years") 2026-06-11 09:00:03 | ✔ | Check passed: NA ids | 0 rows 2026-06-11 09:00:03 | ! | Negative amounts | 3 rows | log/violations/20260611_090003_Negative_amounts.csv 2026-06-11 09:00:04 | ✔ | Check passed: Duplicate person-years | 0 rows tryCatch(   df |> expect_none(is.na(id), abort_msg = "NA ids"),   expectr_failure = \(e) {     saveRDS(e$violations, "na_ids.rds")     stop(e)   } )

title: Assert that a panel is balanced, or has no gaps — expect_balanced
text: Register populations rarely fully balanced: people born, die migrate, firms open close. gaps_only = TRUE relaxes rule usually hold: unit may enter late leave early, present must skip period first last. person present 2019 2021 missing 2020 gap; person first seen 2021 .

title: Assert that a panel is balanced, or has no gaps — expect_balanced
text: default expected periods observed anywhere data. period missing every unit (e.g. year never loaded) therefore invisible. Pass periods expect, e.g. periods = 2015:2024, catch . Observations outside periods ignored, rows missing period. Duplicated unit-periods make panel unbalanced, usually error : check expect_unique()(data, id, time). check scales full-population registers: unit-period grid built units actually lack period.

code: view_types(..., diff = FALSE, focus = NULL)

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: ... Data frames compare (unquoted), single named list data frames, default output daos::read_files(). list can also spliced !!!. Names inferred expressions passed, taken list. diff Logical. TRUE, columns status "conflict" shown, frames bind produce empty result. see every difference, filter status != "ok" instead. Default: FALSE. focus named character vector expected types, e.g. c(cvr = "chr", year = "int"). supplied, named columns shown, datasets type match (absent column counts mismatch). Returns empty tibble (0 rows) types match, can used checkpoints. Takes precedence diff.

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: tibble column column, status column (see Details) one column per input dataset showing abbreviated type string ("int", "dbl", "chr", "fct", "date", "dttm", ...). NA means column absent dataset.

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
text: type string alone say whether two data frames can stacked: int dbl bind without trouble, column entirely NA (readr reads empty column lgl). column absent one dataset obstacle either, since dplyr::bind_rows() fills NA. real conflict chr vs dbl makes bind fail, forces daos::read_files() fall back character. status column therefore asks question function called : bind? "ok": present everywhere type. "coercible": present everywhere, types differ bind without loss structure (int + dbl, fct + chr, date + dttm, -NA lgl anything). "missing": absent least one dataset, conflict among rest. Typically rename dropped column upstream. "conflict": types combined. Compatibility tested binding zero-row slices column dplyr::bind_rows(), classification follows rules daos::read_files(= "bind").

title: Compare column types across data frames — view_types
code: df1 <- data.frame(x = 1L,  y = "a", z = NA) df2 <- data.frame(x = 1.0, y = 2,   z = "b")  view_types(df1, df2) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   column status    df1   df2   #>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr> #> 1 x      coercible int   dbl   #> 2 y      conflict  chr   dbl   #> 3 z      coercible lgl   chr   view_types(df1, df2, diff = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   column status   df1   df2   #>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr> <chr> #> 1 y      conflict chr   dbl   view_types(df1, df2, focus = c(x = "int", y = "chr")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   column status    df2   #>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> #> 1 x      coercible dbl   #> 2 y      conflict  dbl    # A named list of data frames, e.g. from read_files(): view_types(list(a = df1, b = df2)) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   column status    a     b     #>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr> #> 1 x      coercible int   dbl   #> 2 y      conflict  chr   dbl   #> 3 z      coercible lgl   chr
